newsitem.title: USA: PSCo/SPS merger ready for FERC action.
newsitem.headline: PSCo/SPS merger ready for FERC action.

text.p: Southwestern Public Service Co said its pending merger with Public Service Co of Colorado moved forward last week when a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission administrative law judge certified a settlement agreement between the utilities and FERC intervenors, and said the merger application is ready for the federal commission's review.
Presiding administrative law judge David Harfeld wrote that the certification of the settlement agreement makes the need for an initial decision in the case unnecessary.
He concluded, "The record is sufficient for the commission to make a reasoned determination of the applicants' merger application."

"This action means the merger case now can be considered by the commission itself. The commission had given the judge until January 31 to prepare an initial decision. We are very pleased that step will not be necessary, and we are encouraged that a positive decision has come this early," SPS said.
Plans for the merger were announced in August 1995.
Regulators in Wyoming and Colorado have approved the merger. The Kansas Corporation Commission has granted the companies authority to issue stock of the company being formed, New Century Energies.
Regulatory hearings on the merger have been concluded in Texas and New Mexico; the public utility commissions in those states have not announced their decisions, SPS said.
Pending the federal and state approvals, approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, and other conditions, the merger is targeted for completion in spring 1997.
